items.title: Dominic James "Nick" La Rocca Interview, 1959-10-26
items.q: And so all of them copied from Nick LaRock and admitted.

ctx.x: Yes, I've got others. I don't see it as good as Tiger Rag, but there's one in here that has a very good jazz number. And this Let's Jam It has plausibilities. Even this one that I put out as a popular number can be played in the same idiom that I would play it. And so on. There's nothing to it. Any tune becomes a jazz tune when you put the idioms to it.…

These people tell you it's a great big secret. It's nothing but march time, syncopated. White man's music and not colored. That's all it is. You take the tiger rank, we'll fit in that. You play. Hold that tiger. Hold that tiger. You can do anything you want with it. It's waking up different embellishments on a chord construction. That's all it is. Now these fellas in New Orleans, they play today. You know who they play? I'm going to let you know who they play. They're great. I was nobody. They play Big…

Mr. LaRock, I'm glad you brought Big's name into this. Because I wanted you to tell us a little more about your relationship with him. In your previous statement, you said you thought he was a very great musician.
